evidence.r1: Glass is confined to compare, tool, adjustment and culling controls; metadata and the filmstrip are opaque.
evidence.r2: The expanded adjustment palette replaces the narrow tool surface, with plain selected-state fills inside it.
evidence.r3: Three control surfaces cover comparing, adjusting and rating without decorative glass cards.
evidence.r4: The compare strip, culling bar and expanded palette share one dark frosted appearance.
evidence.r5: No clear variant is apparent; the floating controls use dense dark frosting over the photograph.
evidence.r6: The floating controls remain neutral, including the white Pick action and grey selected states.
evidence.r7: The normal tool and culling surfaces reveal softened photograph colours, unlike their flatter reduced-transparency versions.
evidence.r8: The culling and tool bars are capsules, while compare and adjustment surfaces have fixed rounded corners.
evidence.r9: The inset Edit segment and Pick button fit their enclosing corners without visibly pinched arcs.
evidence.r10: The culling actions use capsule forms and the compact compare segments use rounded rectangles.
evidence.r11: Compare, adjustment and culling each have their own shared background for related controls.
evidence.r12: Text-only compare and rating buttons are separated from the icon tool group; slider labels are not text buttons.
evidence.r13: Glass covers each whole control group rather than the icons, labels or slider thumbs.
evidence.r14: The expanded tools and sliders read as one continuous palette, separate from compare and culling.
evidence.r15: No scroll-edge treatment is visible at the photo-stage controls or filmstrip boundary.
evidence.r16: Every floating material surface sits over the detailed forge photograph.
evidence.r17: The tool palette and expanded adjustment panel cover the selected photograph, including the hand and work area.
evidence.r18: White text is legible on the dark controls, but the captures do not establish contrast in a light appearance.
evidence.r19: Reduced transparency preserves the editor layout, but increased contrast and reduced motion are not demonstrated.
evidence.r20: The photograph is inset within dark margins beside a hard-edged metadata sidebar rather than reaching the window edges.
evidence.r21: The stage stops at dark gutters and the metadata sidebar, with no visible background extension.
evidence.r22: The floating control surfaces have no separate visible backing plate or local darkening scrim beneath them.
evidence.r23: The expanded palette is shown only after opening, so its transition and pointer feedback cannot be judged.
evidence.r24: Tool icons, compare labels, ratings and slider controls are monochrome.
evidence.r25: White control labels remain separated from the photographic colours by the dark material.
